body:
The session added one number to a turn end: the turn-ended event data gains the key scheduled_wakes, the count of the session's scheduled wakes, beside background_tasks.
The count is the length of the claude Stop payload's session_crons array alone; no element is read and no wake content crosses; it is null when absent, null or not an array, and null on an API-error (StopFailure) turn end.
It reaches the hops background_tasks reaches and no others: the turn-ended event line, CLI wait --json and the MCP wait tool's structured content; not last, list, the snapshot or the replay.
No human-readable output changed: no CLI line, caption, refusal, hint, colour or terminal byte; wait still wakes on a turn end exactly as before.
No new event kind, IPC method, endpoint, socket, env var, config key, crate or dependency; nothing retired; the live reading of a real wake was not run and stays a carry on the standing live rig entry.

body_fields.what: the internal core crate's event kind table, the closed list of each event kind's data keys; turn-ended now names four keys
the claude hook normaliser, the single vendor-content boundary that maps a claude Stop or StopFailure hook payload to turn-ended event data, with its unit tests
the wait job, which events wake a parked viola wait driver, with its unit tests
the state crate's event-log suite, the check that a turn-ended data key is a known key
the MCP server tool handler suite, the MCP wait tool's structured content
the hook-event integration suite, a booted wrapper fed recorded claude hook payloads, with the no-content scan of every home file
the viola wait and viola last CLI suite, wait --json output of a turn end
the human-takes-the-wheel CLI suite; one line added to a recorded turn-end fixture it feeds

body: decision/single-vendor-content-boundary: the claude hook boundary now reads one more vendor field, session_crons, as a length only; no vendor content crosses, the rule holds and gains a second count-only field.
decision/critical-path-cli-board-output: the wait/last output critical path; wait --json of a turn end now carries scheduled_wakes, while the human wait and last output is unchanged.
contract/viola-wait/waiting-line and contract/viola-wait/timed-out: viola wait output; the waking rule and its human lines are unchanged, only the --json turn-end document gains a key.
contract/mcp-wait-tool/timeout-ms: the MCP wait tool; its structured content of a turn end now carries scheduled_wakes unchanged, its timeout bound untouched.
decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver and decision/no-unwarned-timeouts: a wait driver's bound; wait wakes on a turn end whatever its scheduled_wakes, no bound moved and no timer added.
decision/no-assertions-for-internal-crates: the core crate's event kind table changed; its pin is a crate test, not an a11y assertion.
decision/a11y-inside-existing-suites and decision/a11y-runs-in-existing-test-suites: seven new tests landed inside existing suites; no new suite, driver or a11y artifact.
decision/live-readings-never-gate: the live reading of a fired scheduled wake was not run and is carried on the standing live rig entry; nothing gates on it.
decision/boundary-check-never-inspects-claude-content and decision/no-screen-content-parsing: the new field is read from the hook payload, never from the screen, and its elements are not inspected.
decision/paths-not-carried and decision/control-character-escaping: the new value is a bare integer or null, carrying no path and no printable text to escape.
decision/fixed-cli-strings-pinned and decision/fixed-cli-strings-pinned-by-literal: the wait and wheel suites' literal pins of human output still hold unchanged; only a fixture line was added.
The board and list rows (caption, order, colour, stale row, unwrapped separator, NAME truncation): no list output changed and the count does not reach list.
Refusal, fault and exit-code rows (unable and hint lines, code words, exit codes 2 to 21, --json failure documents, instance-unreachable details): no refusal or code word was added or moved.
The TUI passthrough rows and the keyboard harness rows (human keystrokes, the wheel, terminal bytes, focus, mouse and resize sequences, vt100 feed panic): no terminal byte or stdin rule changed.
Colour and SGR rows (amber DIALOG, bold NAME, dim stale, no SGR off a terminal, word beside every SGR): no styled output changed.
Screen-reader and manual pass rows (Orca targets, manual keyboard pass), and the absences (web frontend, touch, i18n, user time limit): the session reaches none.
CI and gate rows (fail-fast gate, zero flakiness, coverage and doctest, GitHub Actions workflow, structured violation JSON): no gate, threshold or CI leg changed.
viola revive, link, unlink, plugin install, verify and help rows: none of those commands or their output changed.

The turn-ended event data gains a fourth key, scheduled_wakes: a count of the session's scheduled wakes beside background_tasks, one number and no content.
The count is the length of the Stop hook payload's session_crons array; null when the key is absent, null or not an array, and a non-array writes a drift entry to the instance detail file only, as background_tasks does.
An API-error (StopFailure) turn end writes scheduled_wakes null beside its null last_assistant_message and background_tasks and its cause.
The key reaches exactly the hops background_tasks reaches: the turn-ended line in events.ndjson, CLI wait --json and MCP wait structuredContent unchanged; not last, list, the snapshot or the replay.
wait wakes on a turn end as before, whatever its scheduled_wakes; no new IPC method, event kind, endpoint, env var, crate or protocol version bump (v unchanged, an additive field).
Measured: the recorded Stop fixtures carry an empty session_crons and now read 0; a live session reading 1 with a wake scheduled is unmeasured and carried to the standing live rig entry.

body: The contract row event data turn-ended last_assistant_message: it says the data carries no scheduled-wake count and lists data as last_assistant_message, background_tasks, cause?; now false and stale, the data is last_assistant_message, background_tasks, scheduled_wakes, cause?.
The contract row event data turn-ended background_tasks: a sibling item for scheduled_wakes is owed beside it (same hops, same null rules, same drift entry).

The contract row channel methods wait wake kinds (and channel wait method wake kinds): a turn end wakes whatever its background_tasks or scheduled_wakes; the wake rule itself is unchanged but the row's wording names one key only.
The contract row Hook to kind map StopFailure: its enumeration of the null data on an API-error turn end gains scheduled_wakes null.
The contract row Hook to kind map Stop: the Stop payload now also reads session_crons, by length alone, into turn-ended data.
The contract row normalised event kinds turn-ended: its data key set moved from three keys to four, no new kind.

Rules over the agent-neutral event kind table and its data keys (event kinds added only in viola-core, the unknown-field count of the event reader): a key was added to an existing kind there, not a new kind.

Rules over the Claude hook payload parse: external payloads parsed tolerantly, unparseable external values become unknown, missing and null read the same, Claude payload shapes in one crate, upstream text untrusted and content-bearing detail only in the instance; the new session_crons field follows each (null when absent or not an array, a drift entry in the instance detail file, no element read).
Rules over what reaches the MCP wait and CLI wait --json documents, and the MCP tools wait contract item: the turn-ended data they pass through now holds scheduled_wakes.
The protocol version bump rule and versioned-tolerant own formats: the change is an additive data field with v unchanged, which those rows must still admit.
JSON field names in snake_case: scheduled_wakes is a new wire key under that convention, the CLI's session_crons name kept out of viola's own data.

body_fields.fact: turn-ended data carries scheduled_wakes, the count of the session's scheduled wakes (the Stop payload's session_crons length alone, no element read), null when the key is absent, null or not an array, a non-array writing a drift entry to the instance detail file only, null on an API-error turn end; it reaches the events.ndjson line, CLI wait --json and MCP wait only, not last, list, the snapshot or the replay.
A turn end wakes wait whatever its scheduled_wakes, as whatever its background_tasks; a scheduled wake is counted, never a wake condition.

body:
The session added one key, scheduled_wakes, to the turn-ended event data: the count of the session's scheduled wakes, a number or null, never their content.
The hook reads the Stop payload's session_crons array as its length alone, no element read and none redacted or kept; null when the key is absent, null or not an array; null on an API-error (StopFailure) turn end.
A non-array session_crons writes a drift entry {path session_crons, expected array} to the instance detail file only, as background_tasks already does.
The count reaches the hops background_tasks reaches and no others: the turn-ended line in the event stream, CLI wait --json and the MCP wait tool's structured result; not last, list, the snapshot or replay. wait's wake rule is unchanged.
No new IPC method, event kind, log field, parse-rejected word, diagnostics schema word, config key, env var, crate or dependency; turn-ended data goes from three keys to four, an additive field with its version unchanged.
Measured: the recorded Stop fixtures carry an empty session_crons and now read 0; that a live session reads 1 with a wake scheduled is unmeasured and carried to the standing live rig.

the wrapper's wait dispatch, which kinds of event wake a parked wait
the state crate's event-log tests, the known-key and unknown-field checks over written events

body: The drift-report decisions (drift reports go to the detail file only) and the detail-file line's drift_report field gain a second count-only field, session_crons, whose wrong-type drift entry lands in the instance detail file only.

The rows that keep the assistant message and other turn content out of logs and home-level files: the new key carries a count alone, no wake prompt, schedule or id, and a planted canary in the wake content is scanned absent from every home file.
The event stream line and its shape: the turn-ended line carries one more data key, scheduled_wakes, additive with the line version unchanged.
The viola-mcp wait tool contract: its structured result carries the turn end's scheduled_wakes count unchanged beside background_tasks.
The rows keeping event payloads out of process logs: the new count rides the event stream and wait results only, and no process log line or diagnostics field gains it.
Type-level redaction of payload types: the new hook stdin field holds ignored elements and its length only, so it carries no redaction marker and keeps no text.
The wait log line's outcome and the wait path's events: unchanged, since wait wakes on a turn end whatever its scheduled_wakes, as it does whatever its background_tasks.
Recorded fixtures as no telemetry source: the recorded Stop fixtures were read, not changed, and their empty session_crons now reads 0.
The content canary rule (never in home-level files, only in detail files): extended by a booted case over the scheduled-wake content.

body:
A turn end now carries the session's scheduled-wake count beside its background-task count: one number, no content.
The turn-ended event data gains the key scheduled_wakes, the length of the Stop hook payload's session_crons array; null when the key is absent, null or not an array; null on an API-error (StopFailure) turn end.
No element of the array is read or kept; a non-array value writes one drift entry to the instance diagnostics detail file only, as background_tasks does.
The count reaches the same hops background_tasks reaches (the turn-ended line in the event log, CLI wait --json, MCP wait structuredContent) and no others; wait wakes on a turn end as before.
No new channel method, endpoint, event kind, socket, port, env var, crate, dependency, config key or schema file; nothing retired.
Measured from recorded fixtures only: a recorded Stop with an empty session_crons now reads 0; a live session reading 1 with a wake scheduled is unmeasured and carried as a PROVISIONAL live-rig reading.

body_fields.what: edited — the core crate's shared contract types: the event kind table and each kind's closed list of known data keys, which the event log reader checks unknown fields against

edited — the Claude adapter's hook payload normaliser: the tolerant parse of hook stdin into known fields, the drift entries for a field of the wrong type, and the mapping of Stop and StopFailure payloads to turn-ended event data
edited — the wrapper's wait verb: which events wake a parked wait and what a turn end's data carries back to the driver
edited — the state crate's event log reader tests: known-key and unknown-field checks over written event lines
edited — the MCP server's tool handler tests: the wait tool's structuredContent passed through unchanged
edited — the booted end-to-end hook tests: a hook payload through the wrapper into events, with a planted-canary scan of every home file for content that must not be kept
edited — the CLI wait and last end-to-end tests: the --json document a driver reads back from a turn end
edited — the CLI wheel end-to-end tests: the turn-ended data a wheel test asserts on, human output unchanged

body: decision/stop-background-tasks-count-only: its sibling is owed — Stop's session_crons now crosses the hook boundary the same way, as a length only, no element read, null when absent, null or not an array, a non-array writing a drift entry.
decision/api-error-turn-end-text-dropped: stale — an API-error turn end now carries null last_assistant_message, null background_tasks and null scheduled_wakes beside its cause.

decision/hook-payload-is-content and decision/tolerant-hook-parsing: the hook payload's session_crons elements (wake ids, schedules, prompts) are content; the tolerant parse now reads one more field, its length only, ignoring every element.
decision/drift-reports-diagnostics-only: a new drift entry path session_crons expected array goes to the instance diagnostics detail file only, never to the event data.
decision/hook-security-fields-closed and decision/hook-security-fields-closed-enums: a new hook field is read; it is a count, not a security field, and its drift word is array.

decision/user-content-only-to-diagnostics, decision/never-log-claude-values and decision/upstream-text-is-content: no wake prompt or schedule text reaches events, snapshot or logs; a booted test scans every home file for a planted canary.

contract/mcp-tools/wait and contract/wrapper-channel-methods/wait: the wait reply's turn-ended data carries one more key, scheduled_wakes; the wake rule is unchanged and MCP structuredContent passes it unchanged.

decision/shared-validators-in-core and decision/closed-types-for-protocol-fields: the core crate's closed list of turn-ended data keys grows from three to four (last_assistant_message, background_tasks, scheduled_wakes, cause optional).
decision/api-error-classes-adapter-only: the StopFailure arm of the Claude adapter now also writes scheduled_wakes null; the class words stay inside the adapter.
decision/question-option-text-crosses-boundary: any row listing what of a hook payload crosses into events now has one more crossing, a bare count.

body_fields.fact: Stop's session_crons crosses the hook boundary as its length alone, scheduled_wakes on turn-ended: no element read or kept, null when absent, null or not an array, a non-array writing one drift entry to the diagnostics detail file; null on an API-error turn end.
The scheduled-wake count reaches only the hops the background-task count reaches (the turn-ended event line, CLI wait --json, MCP wait); last, list, the snapshot and the replay do not carry it.

The unit contract on dialog and Stop event data null details (description, preview and background_tasks) owes the scheduled_wakes sibling: null when the Stop payload key is absent or not an array, and null on a StopFailure turn end.

Wait wake-kind contracts (the channel wait method's wake kinds, wait wake kinds, viola wait wake on turn-ended, viola wait turn-ended wake): a turn end wakes whatever its background_tasks or scheduled_wakes; the rule is unchanged but a row that enumerates the turn-ended data it returns now reads one more key.

Unknown hook payload fields tolerated and harness or tolerant event reader rows: session_crons moves from an ignored unknown Stop field to a known one read by length only, and scheduled_wakes is a known key, unknown_fields 0.

CLI and MCP return identical payloads: CLI wait --json and MCP wait structuredContent both carry scheduled_wakes unchanged.

viola last newest turn message and the last document: last does not carry scheduled_wakes; a row asserting the last document's key set holds.
